description: Everything the content library holds and everything produced from it. Source material and generated pieces live in one index so reuse is visible — the second-best outcome of a request is finding something that already answers it.

columns.name: path
columns.note: Relative path from the project root

columns.name: is_source
columns.note: yes = library material to build FROM. no = something produced for a specific deal.

columns.name: library_section
columns.note: For source assets: Corporate or Product, matching 02-Context/Presentations/

columns.name: audience_type
columns.note: Drives register and depth far more than industry does

columns.name: audience_names
columns.note: Actual people it was written for, when known

columns.name: built_from
columns.note: ASSET ids of source material used, semicolon-separated

columns.name: competitor_id
columns.note: COMP- id when the piece positions against a named competitor

columns.name: signals_used
columns.note: SIG- ids whose news is referenced. Lets you find what to correct if a signal turns out wrong.

columns.name: request_origin
columns.note: What prompted it. 'Customer ask' pieces get used; proactive ones often don't — worth knowing which is which.

columns.name: request_detail
columns.note: What they actually asked for, in their words where possible

columns.name: unverified_claims
columns.note: Anything asserted that could not be confirmed from the context library or a source. MUST be filled where relevant — this is what gets checked before the piece goes to a customer.

columns.name: gaps_flagged
columns.note: What the requester still needs to supply or confirm

columns.name: outcome_note
columns.note: What happened after it was sent. The only way the library learns.
